subject: Television & Streaming
title: What a Showrunner Actually Does
description: A micro-lesson that makes What a Showrunner Actually Does usable.

hook.text: A film has a director. A TV show has a showrunner—part writer, part CEO, part therapist for an entire production.

buildup.text: The showrunner manages scripts, budgets, casting, editing, and network relationships. Every decision flows through them.

discovery.text: In film, the director is king. In television, the writer is king. Showrunners are almost always writers first.

twist.text: The job didn't even have a name until the 1990s. For decades, the person running the show had no official title.

climax.text: Today, showrunners are the most powerful people in television. They shape what millions of viewers see every week.

punchline.text: The most powerful job in TV didn't have a name until recently.
